title: Make the test host answer like the real one

blocks.text: The client's integration tests run against `HostSimulator`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/HostSimulator.java`, instead of the acquirer's host. The simulator should answer exactly as the host's interface document says: the response MTI, the fields listed in `ECHOED`, a response code, and an approval code on approvals. The tests keep every request they send, so that they can check afterwards what the client asked for.
`respond` is written. Finish the two methods it calls, marked `TODO`:

When you're done, every kind of request the client sends, first attempts and repeats, gets the response type the real host would send, a response never carries a field the document doesn't list, and the request a test kept still reads as the client sent it. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a purchase and an authorization are answered with the response MTI, the echoed fields and the response code
a repeat and an advice are answered with the response MTI of a first attempt, such as 0230 for an 0221
a response carries only the listed fields, so card and chip data the request carried never come back
answering a request leaves the request as the client sent it

origin.section: 6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

concepts: A follow-up copies the fields it lists with clone(int...) and leaves the original unchanged; copying all and pruning leaks what was forgotten.
setResponseMTI answers a repeat with the response of a first attempt and refuses a response.
